blocks.text: Most human diseases result from microbial infections: invasions of the body by viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi or protists. To defend against infections and against cancers, vertebrates have the immune system, which continually checks the bloodstream for foreign cells and molecules. When it detects an infection it attacks and destroys the invaders; that is why diseases that weaken it, such as AIDS, are so dangerous.

blocks.alt: Three coloured columns joined by arrows. 1st line, non-specific barriers: skin, mucous membranes, acid, lysozyme and cilia. 2nd line, non-specific, inside the body: germ-killer cells, protective proteins, inflammation and fever. 3rd line, specific immune system: T cells, B cells and antibodies, memory.
blocks.caption: The three lines of defence (original diagram after Figure 21.1).
blocks.long_description: The body has three lines of defence. The first, the skin and the linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts with their acid, lysozyme, mucus and cilia, keeps microbes out. Microbes that get through meet the second line: germ-killer cells, protective proteins, inflammation and fever. These two lines are non-specific, acting against any invader. The third line, the immune system of T cells, B cells and antibodies, is specific: it targets particular germs and remembers them, so it responds faster the next time.

blocks.title: Tidbit: a defended city
blocks.text: The body is defended like a city against invasion: walls make entry difficult, roaming police check strangers, and security guards challenge anyone without proper identification and call the police. The body likewise has several lines of defence.
The first line of defence consists of the skin, the digestive tract and the respiratory tract.

blocks.prompt: What does the first line of defence consist of?
blocks.explanation: The skin and the linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts.

items: Immune system defends against infections and cancers.
Three lines: barriers, non-specific internal defences, specific immunity.
